Separation in multinomial, conditional and rank-ordered logit data

Source: R/separation.R
separation.Rd

Checks whether the data of an mnl() or rologit() fit are separated, so that the maximum-likelihood estimates do not exist. Each observation reports that some alternatives are preferred to others: the choice to every other available alternative, or, in a ranking, each alternative of a rank group to each of the next (ties as groups, the unranked alternatives last). A finite maximum-likelihood estimate exists if and only if no direction of the coefficients weakly favours every one of these comparisons and strictly favours at least one (overlap; Albert and Anderson 1984 for logistic regression, Speckman, Lee and Sun 2009 for choice models, Sablica, Hornik and Rusch 2026 for rankings). Along such a direction the log-likelihood rises towards its supremum and the estimates run off. Overlap is first sought by a certificate: positive weights on the comparisons that balance them exactly (Stiemke's lemma), built from the fitted probabilities at the fit's estimates, where the gradient of the log-likelihood is such a weighted sum (not for tied rankings). Otherwise the check solves a linear program (lp_solve, through lpSolveAPI). Both are exact up to floating-point tolerances.

Usage

separation(object)

Arguments

object

A fit from mnl() or rologit(), without unit fixed effects or inflation (maximum likelihood or penalized: separation is a property of the data and the model, not of the fit).

Value

An object of class polychoice_separation: separated (logical); type ("overlap", "quasi-complete", or "complete": every comparison separated); terms, the coefficients that move along some separating direction (a term can have a zero coordinate in the reported direction and still move along another); direction, a separating direction (unit length; along it every comparison some separating direction can favour is favoured); cases, the identifiers of the cases with a separated comparison; n_comparisons (all the comparisons the data report), n_separated, n_zero (the comparisons with identical design rows, up to rounding); and method, "certificate" or "linear program".

Details

The maximum-likelihood fits of mnl() and rologit() (without unit fixed effects or inflation) run this check and name the diverging coefficients in a warning; penalized fits (firth = TRUE or a prior) store them in separation, and summary() marks them [sep]. The other estimators judge divergence by the size of a coefficient and its Wald statistic.

A comparison between two alternatives with the same design row in a case (possible without alternative-specific constants), or with rows that differ only by rounding (each attribute's difference within 64 machine epsilons of the larger of its two values and the attribute's typical size, the median of its nonzero absolute values; such as attributes computed as 0.1 + 0.2 and 0.3, centred or not), is favoured by no direction. It is counted (n_zero), and with one the data are at most quasi-completely separated, since that choice's probability stays below one along every direction.

References

Albert, A. and Anderson, J.A. (1984). On the existence of maximum likelihood estimates in logistic regression models. Biometrika, 71, 1-10. doi:10.1093/biomet/71.1.1

Sablica, L., Hornik, K. and Rusch, T. (2026). The geometry of existence and uniqueness of maximum likelihood estimation in categorical response models. arXiv:2610.08100.

Speckman, P.L., Lee, J. and Sun, D. (2009). Existence of the MLE and propriety of posteriors for a general multinomial choice model. Statistica Sinica, 19, 731-748.

Examples

data(defection)
## Cook, Niehaus and Zuhlke's Model 3: no captured combatant joined for
## economic reasons without being indoctrinated (an empty cell)
m3 <- mnl(outcome ~ economic * indoctrination + age_joined + birth_year + school_age + male,
          data = defection, ref = "captured", firth = TRUE)
#> The maximum-likelihood estimates of demobilized:economic, demobilized:economic:indoctrination, switched:economic, switched:economic:indoctrination diverge (separation); their penalized estimates are determined largely by the penalty. Profile penalized-likelihood intervals (confint()) and penalized likelihood-ratio tests are the recommended inference.
separation(m3)
#> Quasi-complete separation: 15 of the 1164 comparisons the data report are separated, in 15 case(s);
#> the maximum-likelihood estimates do not exist.
#> Coefficients moving along some separating direction (the reported direction's coordinates):
#>                demobilized:economic demobilized:economic:indoctrination 
#>                                 0.5                                -0.5 
#>                   switched:economic    switched:economic:indoctrination 
#>                                 0.5                                -0.5
